title: KV granule lease and live relocation protocol for reducing GPU memory fragmentation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: As continuous batching increases request throughput, the KV cache on GPUs accumulates small-lived and long-lived token entries that fragment device memory over time. Current coarse page reclamation causes scheduling spikes and increased tail latency during background compaction. This ticket designs and implements a lease-driven 'granule' allocation + live relocation protocol to reduce fragmentation without hurting latency SLOs.

Goals:
- Reduce long-term fragmentation metric (ROSTM: residual occupied small extents) by >= 40% in 72-hour steady-state workload.
- Keep p99 generation latency increase <= 3% when relocation runs concurrently with batching.
- Provide observability: per-granule hotness heatmaps, relocation throughput, and token-preserving remap counters.

Design summary:
1) Granule abstraction: allocate KV entries into variable-sized "granules" (4–64 KB logical ranges) grouped by observed token lifespan and access hotness. Granules are the unit of relocation/eviction instead of individual cache slots.
2) Lease mechanism: each granule is assigned a short lease (100–500ms) renewed on active use. Leases allow background workers to identify cold granules safe for relocation without pausing serving threads.
3) Live relocation: background workers perform token-preserving remap: move entries from cold granules into compacted target granules and update an indirection table atomically. Continuous batching paths read indirection first, ensuring no synchronous pause.
4) Shadow-eviction and validation: before committing relocation we keep a shadow copy for one batching tick to validate no re-hits caused by concurrent requests. If re-hit occurs, relocation is aborted and granule hotness is bumped.
5) Placement policy: prefer co-locating short-lifespan granules together to create reclaimable islands, and pin very hot granules to dedicated hot lanes to avoid churn.
6) Heuristics and telemetry: heat decay uses exponential windows tuned by observed sequence lengths; track fragmentation ratio, relocation abort rate, average relocation time, and batching interference metric.

Trade-offs considered:
- Fine-grained per-token compaction minimizes memory waste but increases metadata overhead and synchronization; granule-level trades slightly higher residual waste for lower coordination cost.
- Lease durations: shorter leases reduce false cold detection but increase lease renewals; chosen conservative defaults with auto-tuning based on request inter-arrival distribution.
- Shadow validation adds memory overhead but significantly reduces correctness bugs in early experiments.

Implementation plan:
- Phase 1 (PoC): implement granule metadata and lease state transitions in the runtime, plus unit tests for atomic indirection updates. (ENG-802357-POC PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1432)
- Phase 2 (Canary): wire background relocation worker, shadow validation, and expose metrics to the Console; run canary on dedicated pool with synthetic churn workloads.
- Phase 3 (Scale): rollout to mixed-hosting with gradual traffic ramp and automatic tuning of lease window and granule sizing.

Metrics and validation:
- New metrics: kv_granule_free_ratio, kv_relocation_abort_rate, kv_lease_renewals_per_sec, kv_relocation_latency_ms histogram, kv_indirection_updates_total.
- Regression tests: p99 latency under continuous batching trace, 72-hour fragmentation soak test against real customer-like prompt distributions.
- Acceptance criteria: fragmentation drop >= 40% at steady-state, relocation abort < 1% under normal load, p99 latency regression < 3%.

Rollout & safety controls:
- Feature flag gated, with runtime knobs to disable relocation per-server.
- Canary schedules: 0.1% -> 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with health checks at each step.
- Fallback: automatic disable if kv_relocation_abort_rate > 5% or p99 latency spikes > 5% for 10m.

Open questions / risks:
- Interaction with GPU memory allocator: need to coordinate with device allocator to avoid double-copy spikes when migrating hot granules. Follow-up ticket planned to add device-level async memcpy throttling.
- Accurate hotness scoring for multi-model shared pools where cross-customer noise exists. We'll add tenant-aware heuristics in a later iteration.
